messages:
alan: Quick thread: we need to pick a long-term pattern for Private CP connectivity. Two options on the table: (A) regional CP-edge broker that multiplexes many customers behind a thin relay in each region, or (B) per-customer VPC endpoints / PrivateLink equivalents with direct controlplane peering. Want to call out failure modes, ops cost, and migration friction.

sophia: TL;DR my gut: broker = cheaper infra ops but bigger blast radius; per-customer endpoints = more infra/cost but clearer isolation and easier customer ownership.

mike: Agree. Also want to highlight DNS & cert distribution differences. Broker model can terminate TLS at our regional fleet and present a single cert per-customer virtual hostname. Endpoint model needs routes + certs bound inside customer VPC.

claire: Two other constraints: 1) some customers require egress / no inbound peering (i.e., agent must dial out). 2) regulated customers want no shared-controlplane compute inside their networks. Those push toward per-customer endpoint or a thin customer-managed relay.

alan: Failure scenarios I care about: (1) regional broker outage -> many customers impacted; (2) route flap / peering churn on per-customer endpoints -> noisy ops; (3) cross-account route exhaustion if we scale ENIs per customer.

sophia: Ops/Cost tradeoff: broker requires beefy autoscaling & robust isolation (per-tenant rate limiting, soft CPU qdisc). But network egress cost may be lower because we centralize on optimized uplinks. Endpoints mean more ENIs and NATs to manage per-account, raising cloud bill.

mike: Latency: broker adds one hop -> small RTT but easier to optimize (local caches, warm KV). Endpoint directness can be lower latency for customers colocated in region, but it adds complexity on rollout / version skew.

claire: Security/Compliance: broker model needs stronger tenancy isolation (sandboxing) and attestable logging so we can prove no data commingling. Endpoint model is simpler to argue for customers since compute isn't shared.

alan: Migration UX: Broker = easiest to migrate existing Private endpoints (flip DNS and handshake), Endpoint = likely needs infra changes in customer accounts (IAM, attachments). For customers on Dedicated or Private, endpoint rollout is more friction.

ops-bot: note: cost simulation for 500 customers shows per-customer endpoints ~ +35% network infra spend vs broker (preliminary). See https://go/cost-sims/privcp-500

mike: Edge case: multi-region customers who want controlplane affinity per-region. Broker can route to nearest cluster, but per-customer endpoints require provisioning in each region. More ops complexity but better locality.

sophia: Compromise proposal: adopt broker as default for self-serve customers, and offer per-customer endpoint or dedicated relay as an enterprise opt-in. Also support a "customer-managed relay" container they can run in their VPC that tunnels to our broker for telemetry only.

claire: For the broker we must define strong failure isolation: per-tenant circuit breakers, CPU/mem limits, and per-tenant quotas persisted in control plane. Also logging segregated per tenant and available for export to customer via S3 or remote syslog.

alan: Implementation steps I propose:
1) Spike: broker proof-of-concept with per-customer soft isolation + eviction policy (5d).
2) Spike: automated endpoint provisioning playbook & IAM templates (3d).
3) Security review + compliance checklist for broker tenancy guarantees (2d).
4) Migration plan doc mapping current private endpoints -> broker cutover (1w).

mike: Add: e2e test scenario: simulated broker outage and per-customer endpoint failover. Measure RTO and impact surface.

ops-bot: created: RFC 2042 "regional-cp-broker-vs-direct-endpoints" assigned: alan, sophia, mike. Link: https://go/rfc/2042

sophia: :thumbsup: I'll draft the matrix comparing isolation, cost, latency, onboarding friction, test coverage, and rollback plan.

claire: Final ask: include actionable SLO/SLI differences in RFC. A shared broker may need stricter per-tenant SLAs to prevent noisy neighbors.

alan: Will do. Thanks all. We can iterate in RFC comments. :wave:
